clue.text: Plot to get drug for old monk

parts.note: a garden plot or flower bed
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A schemer plans to obtain narcotics for an elderly friar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plot' looks like a verb meaning scheme, but it is a garden bed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Venerable Bede was an Anglo-Saxon monk and historian of the eighth century.

clue.text: Deadly virus hard to shift around centre of Vienna

indicators.note: around says the rearranged letters go on either side of the next piece
to shift something is to move it, so these letters move into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

indicators.note: the centre is the middle, so only the core letters of the following word are used

parts.note: the two central letters of the six-letter city name

explanation.surface: A lethal virus proves difficult to dislodge from central Vienna.
explanation.walkthrough: Hendra is a real virus, named after a Brisbane suburb, that passes from bats to horses and humans.
explanation.definitionFit: Hendra virus is a highly lethal pathogen first identified in Australia in 1994, often fatal to humans.

clue.text: Support my clue Angel oddly rejected for 'flammable gas'

parts.note: a prop is a support

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters are thrown away, so only the even ones remain

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters of these words run together

explanation.surface: A setter asks for backing after an angelic clue of theirs was oddly turned down for describing a gas.
explanation.walkthrough: Run 'my clue Angel' together as one string before keeping its even letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Propylene, or propene, is a colourless hydrocarbon gas that burns readily and is used to make plastics.

clue.text: Spooner's enthusiastic girlfriend makes vegetarian food

indicators.note: Rev. Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts of the two words trade places

parts.note: enthusiastic is keen and bird is slang for a girlfriend; swap their initial sounds

explanation.surface: An eager partner cooks a meat-free dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: Bird is British slang for a girlfriend; swapping the K and B sounds of KEEN BIRD gives BEAN CURD.
explanation.definitionFit: Bean curd, or tofu, is pressed soya-milk curd and a staple protein of meatless cooking.

clue.text: Conservative Party left-winger taken into account

parts.note: standard abbreviation
a side is a party in a dispute
a red is a socialist or communist

explanation.surface: A left-wing member of the Conservative Party has been taken into consideration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' looks political alongside Conservative, but here it means one side in a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: Something considered has been weighed up and thought about, which is to say allowed for.

clue.text: Decorator presses buzzer to get drink

indicators.note: to press something is to hug or squeeze it, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: one who ices cakes decorates them
a bee buzzes

explanation.surface: A painter rings a doorbell to obtain a beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decorator' suggests a house painter, but here it is someone who ices cakes, and the buzzer is an insect, not a bell.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice beer is lager brewed with a freezing stage that removes some water, raising its strength.

clue.text: The neighbour of Violet Jones, the architect, collects diamonds

indicators.note: to collect something is to gather it in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: Inigo Jones was a seventeenth-century English architect
D is the card abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: Next door to a woman called Violet lives an architect named Jones who collects gems.
explanation.walkthrough: Violet reads as a woman's name, but it is the colour, and its neighbour is the one before it in the rainbow.
explanation.definitionFit: In the spectrum's colour order, indigo sits directly beside violet at the short-wavelength end.

clue.text: When do old cooks dance?

indicators.note: to cook something is to doctor or falsify it, so the letters are tampered with

parts.note: taken as written
O is the standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A question about when elderly chefs take to the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooks' reads as a noun in the question, but it is a verb acting on the letters before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoedown is a lively American folk gathering with square dancing, or the dance itself.

clue.text: He lives in torment

parts.note: taken as written
L stands for live, as on electrical wiring, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A man exists in a state of constant agony.
explanation.walkthrough: Doubling a letter abbreviation makes a plural, as with pp for pages.
explanation.definitionFit: Hell is used loosely for any state of great suffering or anguish, as in 'living hell'.

clue.text: Leading revolutionary has brief look at African capital

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns right round, so this word is read backwards

parts.note: main means chief or leading

indicators.note: being brief means being cut short, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: to eye something is to look at it

explanation.surface: A rebel leader glances quickly at a city in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading revolutionary' suggests a figure like Che or Mao, but revolutionary just turns the word for leading round.
explanation.definitionFit: Niamey is the capital city of Niger in West Africa, on the river Niger.

clue.text: Fear breaking card-reader

indicators.note: the word sits inside the next one, as though it breaks through its middle

parts.note: the letters sit across the join of card and reader

explanation.surface: Someone is anxious about a card-reading machine failing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' tempts an anagram, but the answer lies in plain sight within 'card-reader'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dread is a noun for deep apprehension or terror, a straight synonym of fear.

clue.text: Seat of learning regularly infers vicar is in Pacific islands

parts.note: short for polytechnic, a college

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every second letter is kept

parts.note: the even-placed letters of these two words run together

explanation.surface: A college regularly deduces that its chaplain is living out in the South Seas.
explanation.walkthrough: A poly, short for polytechnic, was a British college of higher education until 1992.
explanation.definitionFit: Polynesia is the large group of central and southern Pacific island chains including Hawaii, Samoa and Tonga.

clue.text: Chew this stew briefly, the whole lot

definitions.note: a cryptic pointer to something one chews, standing for a noun

indicators.note: something said briefly is cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: gumbo is a thick Louisiana stew
all means everything

explanation.surface: A diner is told to chew this stew quickly, all of it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the command 'Chew this': the answer is the thing you would chew.
explanation.definitionFit: A gumball is a round piece of chewing gum, typically sold from a coin machine.

clue.text: Formerly a world leader, uninspiring English perhaps lead Italy

parts.note: meh is a slang expression of indifference
standard abbreviation
lead is an example of a metal, flagged by perhaps
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A former statesman is described as a dull Englishman who might lead Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' looks like a verb about governing Italy, but it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Mehemet Ali ruled Egypt in the early nineteenth century and is often called the founder of modern Egypt.

clue.text: Check retrograde public transport's expected to arrive

indicators.note: retrograde means moving backwards, so the word is written back to front

parts.note: a bus is public transport
a train that is due is expected

explanation.surface: A commuter checks whether the backward-running service is due in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Check' reads as a verb for inspecting, but here it means restrain.
explanation.definitionFit: To check is to hold back or restrain, and to subdue is to bring under control.

clue.text: What sleazeball can give people? Respect, he snarled

indicators.note: a snarled thread is tangled, so these letters are knotted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A seedy character growls at people to show him some respect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snarled' looks like a verb of speech, but it means tangled.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone the creeps is an idiom meaning to make them uneasy, which a sleazy person tends to do.

clue.text: Thinkers had to wildly guess

indicators.note: wildly means in an uncontrolled way, so the letters fly into a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The philosophers were forced to speculate without evidence.
explanation.definitionFit: A shot in the dark is an idiom for an attempt made with no real knowledge, a random stab.

clue.text: Work in film, making quilting fabric

parts.note: toil is hard work
taken as written
E.T. is the Spielberg film

explanation.surface: Working in the movies produces a textile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work in film' reads as a career in cinema, but each word is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Toilinet is a woollen cloth with a cotton and silk warp, historically used for quilting and waistcoats.

clue.text: Perhaps 'Fingers' is contemptible figure in underworld

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and the underworld itself
git is British slang for a contemptible person

explanation.surface: A gangster nicknamed Fingers is a despised character in the criminal world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fingers' looks like a crook's nickname; 'figure' hints at numbers too, but the definition is the fingers themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Fingers and toes are digits, so fingers are an example of the answer, flagged by perhaps.

clue.text: Coin found under a Catholic's grave?

definitions.note: a grave is an example of the answer, flagged by the question mark

indicators.note: in a down entry, being under something means coming after it

parts.note: taken as written
standard abbreviation
a cent is a coin

explanation.surface: Money is discovered beneath a Catholic's burial plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grave' reads as a burial place, but it is the grave accent, the backward-sloping mark as in è.
explanation.definitionFit: A grave is one kind of accent mark placed over a letter, alongside acute and circumflex.

clue.text: Claim made by writer of verse with asymmetric feet

parts.note: 'I am' is a claim, as in 'I am Spartacus'
a Bic is a ballpoint pen

explanation.surface: A poet asserts something about lopsided metrical feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writer' suggests the poet, but here it is a pen.
explanation.definitionFit: Iambic verse uses iambs, metrical feet of one unstressed then one stressed syllable, so unequal halves.

clue.text: One of several doctors is funny

parts.note: the prefix co- marks one of a joint group, as in co-author
a medic is a doctor, here one of the doctors

explanation.surface: A member of a medical team turns out to be amusing.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as CO-MEDIC, a fellow doctor working alongside others.
explanation.definitionFit: Comedic means relating to comedy, so humorous or amusing.

clue.text: Farewell heard when mother leaves for Indian city

parts.note: mum is a British word for mother

indicators.note: heard means listened to rather than read, so the spelling follows the sound

parts.note: a short word of parting

explanation.surface: A child says goodbye as their mother sets off for India.
explanation.definitionFit: Mumbai, formerly Bombay, is India's largest city and financial centre on the west coast.

clue.text: Gets rid of Tintin?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: read as tin plus tin, two metal containers

explanation.walkthrough: Tintin is the boy reporter of Hergé's comics, but split it into two tins, plural of a tin container.
explanation.definitionFit: To can someone is slang for to sack them, and tins are the same as metal food containers.

clue.text: With three copies, Penny left one out, which is complex

indicators.note: out means removed, so these letters are taken away

parts.note: a document made in triplicate has three copies
P is the abbreviation for penny
standard abbreviation
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Penny made three copies but omitted one, which is a complicated business.
explanation.walkthrough: Penny looks like a woman's name, but it is the coin; remove P, L and I from IN TRIPLICATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Intricate means having many interconnected parts, so detailed and complicated.

clue.text: Biting insect found in central Georgia

parts.note: mid means middle
GE is the country code for Georgia

explanation.surface: A stinging bug is discovered in the middle of the state of Georgia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' looks like a hidden-word signal, but nothing is concealed; it simply joins the two parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Midges are tiny flies, many of which bite and swarm, notoriously in the Scottish Highlands.

clue.text: University official made Anderson shelters

indicators.note: to shelter something is to keep it inside, so the answer lies within these words

parts.note: the letters span the end of made and the start of Anderson

explanation.surface: A university administrator built wartime air-raid shelters.
explanation.walkthrough: Anderson shelters were small corrugated-iron air-raid shelters dug into British gardens in the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: A dean heads a university faculty or college and oversees its academic affairs.

clue.text: Vendors of storage facilities that can be picked up

indicators.note: picking up a sound means catching it by ear, so the spelling changes but the sound stays

parts.note: cellars are underground storerooms

explanation.surface: Merchants of portable storage units.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' suggests lifting the storage units, but it means heard.
explanation.definitionFit: Vendors are people who sell things, which is exactly what sellers are.

clue.text: Rustic labourer originally thrown out of Nice

indicators.note: being thrown out means ejected, so that letter is removed from the next word

parts.note: nice means pleasant

indicators.note: originally points to the start of the word before it, so only its opening letter counts

parts.note: the opening letter

explanation.surface: A farmhand was at first expelled from the French city of Nice.
explanation.walkthrough: Nice looks like the Riviera city, but it is the adjective; 'Rustic labourer' tempts as a whole definition, though labourer supplies a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, a rustic is a country dweller of humble rank, much like a peasant.
